entities.summary:
The electricity meter, an essential device for measuring electric energy consumption, emerged prominently in the late 19th century as a response to the rapid expansion of electrical infrastructure. Invented by notable figures such as Thomas Edison and subsequently refined by others, the meter became crucial for the burgeoning electric utility industry, facilitating the commercialization of electricity across Europe and North America. By the early 20th century, electricity meters were widely installed in homes and businesses, changing how energy was consumed and billed.

The first commercial electricity meters were introduced in the 1880s, coinciding with Edison's establishment of the first investor-owned electric utility, the Edison Electric Light Company, in 1882 in New York City. These meters enabled consumers to understand their energy usage in kilowatt-hours, providing a basis for charging customers fairly and effectively. The proliferation of electricity meters paralleled the rise of electrical grids and marked a pivotal shift in urban life, transforming how industries operated and how households functioned.

The legacy of the electricity meter is profound; it laid the groundwork for modern energy management and consumption practices. This technological advancement contributed to the electrification of cities, which catalyzed unprecedented economic growth during the 20th century. The introduction of smart meters in the late 20th and early 21st centuries further revolutionized energy consumption by allowing real-time data transmission, fostering a more efficient and sustainable energy landscape.
